summary.en: Colombian forces are confronting intensified attacks by guerrilla groups and dissidents, including a drone strike in Choco that killed two soldiers and a bomb near a military base that killed four civilians, among them a two-month-old infant, with Venezuela reported to have helped carry out the drone strike. The government has responded with a broader offensive, deploying 1,200 troops to the Venezuela border, tightening surrender terms, and revoking the “total peace” approach by reclassifying rebels as non-political actors under a new law. The United Nations has renewed its mission in Colombia, excluding rural reform, and 225 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Colombianske styrker konfronterer intensiverte angrep fra geriljagrupper og dissidenter, inkludert et droneangrep i Choco som drepte to soldater og en bombe nær en militærbase som drepte fire sivile, blant dem et to-måned gammelt spedbarn, med Venezuela rapportert å ha bistått med droneangrepet. Regjeringen har svart med en bredere offensiv, ved å sette inn 1 200 tropper ved Venezuelas grense, skjerpe vilkårene for overgivelse og oppheve «total fred»-politikken ved å omklassifisere opprørerne som ikke-politiske aktører under en ny lov. De forente nasjoner har fornyet sitt oppdrag i Colombia, uten landbruksreform, og 225 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Colombian conflict
background.extract: The Colombian conflict began on May 27, 1964, and is a low-intensity asymmetric war between the government of Colombia, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and far-left guerrilla groups engaged in armed factional hostilities to increase their influence in Colombian territory. Some of the most important international contributors to the Colombian conflict include multinational corporations, the United States, Cuba, and the drug trafficking industry.
